newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan automakers say not hurt by PGM price surge.
newsitem.headline: Japan automakers say not hurt by PGM price surge.

text.p: Japanese automobile makers said on Monday that soaring global platinum and palladium prices have not effected their production of catalytic convertors.
An acute shortage of platinum group metals (PGM), caused by the Russian suspension of PGM sales, has caused prices to skyrocket in recent days.
Platinum is at its highest since 1990, while palladium prices are at a 17-year peak.
"We have a long-term PGM supply contract with a South African producer and other sources in the U.S. and Canada," said an spokesman for Nissan Motor Co Ltd..

"As expectations that PGM prices would rise were widespread at the beginning of this year, we drew up budgets taking into consideration the possibility of a volatile market," the Nissan spokesman said.
The Nissan spokesman added that the high PGM prices had not prompted the company to refrain from making purchases.
Platinum and palladium are used to make catalytic converters which filter harmful gases and particles from auto exhausts.
Last Friday, German catalytic converter maker Degussa said it could face production curbs if the current supply squeeze in the platinum market continues for another three to four weeks.
Other major Japanese automobile makers also said they had not been forced to change plans for catalytic convertor production.
Toyota Motor Corp said it was not suffering a supply shortage because of a long-term PGM contract with a South African producer.

"There are no metals that can be substituted for platinum and palladium at this stage, so we will be forced to buy the metals," said an official with Toyota Tsusyo Corp, a trading arm of Toyota Motor Corp.
"Moreover, we expect exports from Russia to resume soon," the official said.
A spokesman for Honda Motor Corp Ltd also said the company had not considered changing its purchasing patterns or curbing production at this stage.
